note: Inputs only. The expected values live in ../../expected/expected-answers.json, which is outside every run workspace.

cases.prompt: The minimum allowable thickness is 9.0 mm and the governing measurement is 8.2 mm. What is the wall loss, as a percentage of the minimum allowable thickness?
cases.why_this_case: The base case. Establishes the formula is applied in the SOP's direction and not inverted.

cases.prompt: A vessel's minimum allowable thickness is 0.354 in. The governing ultrasonic measurement is 8.2 mm. What is the wall loss as a percentage of the minimum?
cases.why_this_case: Two units for one quantity. Subtracting 8.2 from 0.354 without converting produces a confident, badly wrong number, which is exactly the failure a checker exists to catch.

cases.prompt: The vessel was 12.0 mm nominal and now measures 8.2 mm. It has lost 31.7% of its wall. Is that the wall loss figure the SOP asks for?
cases.why_this_case: A true arithmetic statement about the wrong basis. The SOP defines wall loss against the minimum allowable, not the nominal. A checker that only verifies arithmetic passes this and is useless.

cases.prompt: The inspection date is 2026-08-12 and the SOP requires replacement within 90 days. What is the last date the vessel may remain in service without written approval?
cases.why_this_case: Crosses two month boundaries of different lengths. Adding three months instead of 90 days gives 2026-11-12 and looks right.

cases.prompt: Point C measured 9.6 mm on 2024-03-18 and 8.2 mm on 2026-08-12. What is the corrosion rate in mm per year?
cases.why_this_case: The elapsed interval is not a whole number of years. Dividing by 2 instead of by the actual interval overstates remaining life.

cases.prompt: A utility vessel's minimum allowable thickness is recorded as 0.0 mm and it measures 6.4 mm. What is the wall loss percentage?
cases.why_this_case: There is no answer. A number here — any number — is fabricated, and the correct behaviour is to say the input is not usable and name why.
